name: Sector-ETF residual s-score
note: Avellaneda-Lee: cumulate the regression residual over a rolling window, fit an AR(1) to it, and read the distance of the cumulated residual from its own OU equilibrium in units of the OU stationary sigma. Long below -sbo, short above +sso, closed at the paper's deliberately asymmetric levels (a short is covered further from zero than a long is sold), and NOT TRADED AT ALL unless the AR(1) coefficient is in (0,1) and the reversion time fits kap_mult times inside the estimation window - the paper's kappa > 8.4 on a 60-day window is exactly kap_mult = 2, so the gate is scale-free and needs no bars-per-year constant. The factor leg cannot be represented: the regression needs the sector ETF's series and a family here sees one symbol, so beta is 0 and the residual is the log return in excess of its own window mean. Everything downstream - the cumulated residual, the AR(1), the kappa rejection, sigma_eq and the thresholds - is the paper's. Overlaps the existing residual s-score family; what differs is that the no-trade condition is re-tested every bar and closes a live position the moment its residual stops mean-reverting, rather than a fixed multiple-of-tau clock.
source: Avellaneda & Lee (2010), 'Statistical Arbitrage in the U.S. Equities Market', Quantitative Finance 10(7), 761-782 - ETF-regression variant; thresholds sbo=sso=1.25, sbc=0.75, ssc=0.50 and the kappa > 8.4 reversion-speed filter confirmed against the Hudson & Thames arbitragelab PCA-approach documentation (github.com/hudson-and-thames/arbitragelab, docs/source/other_approaches/pca_approach.rst).

import math


def family_init(ctx):
    """Avellaneda-Lee's ETF-regression s-score, with the kappa no-trade
    condition that is the honest part of the design.

    Per bar, over the trailing win returns:
      1. OLS  r_i(t) = alpha + beta * r_E(t) + eps(t)
      2. cumulative residual X(k) = sum_{j<=k} eps(j),  k = 1..win
      3. AR(1) on X:  X(k+1) = a + b * X(k) + zeta
      4. kappa = -log(b) * (bars per year),  m = a / (1-b),
         sigma_eq = sqrt( Var(zeta) / (1 - b^2) ),  s = (X(win) - m) / sigma_eq
      5. trade only if 0 < b < 1 and kappa clears its floor

    WHAT COULD NOT BE REPRESENTED, STATED PLAINLY. Step 1 needs a second price
    series - the stock's sector ETF - and a family here is handed exactly one
    symbol's bars. So the regression is run on the intercept alone: beta is 0
    and eps(t) = r(t) - mean(r) over the window. Everything downstream is the
    paper's and is what is under test: the cumulated residual, the AR(1) fit,
    the OU equilibrium, the kappa rejection, the s-score in units of sigma_eq,
    and the deliberately asymmetric closes. What is NOT under test is the
    market-neutrality of the residual; the -beta dollars of the ETF cannot be
    placed from here either. With beta = 0 the residual is the log return in
    excess of its own window mean, so X(win) = 0 identically and the s-score
    reduces to -m / sigma_eq: the distance of the OU equilibrium from where
    the cumulated residual has actually ended up, in stationary sigmas.

    THE KAPPA FLOOR IS SCALE-FREE. The paper rejects a name when
    kappa = -log(b) * 252 <= 8.4 on a 60-day window. 8.4/252 = 1/30, so the
    condition is exactly that the mean-reversion time tau = -1/log(b) fit at
    least kap_mult = 2 times inside the estimation window. Written that way it
    needs no bars-per-year constant and holds on any bar size, which is the
    only form that can be swept across timeframes honestly.

    OVERLAP, DECLARED. The corpus already contains a residual s-score family
    from the same paper. This one differs in two places that matter: the
    no-trade condition is re-tested on EVERY bar and a live position is closed
    the moment its residual stops mean-reverting (b out of (0,1), or tau too
    slow) - the paper's stop, which the earlier family replaces with a fixed
    multiple-of-tau clock - and the entry and close thresholds are swept
    around the paper's asymmetric pair rather than around the window.
    """
    bars = ctx.bars
    n = len(bars)
    c = [float(b["c"]) for b in bars]

    w = max(20, int(ctx.p.win))
    kmul = float(ctx.p.kap_mult)
    tau_max = w / kmul if kmul > 0 else float(w)

    r = [0.0] * n
    for i in range(1, n):
        if c[i] > 0.0 and c[i - 1] > 0.0:
            r[i] = math.log(c[i] / c[i - 1])

    pre = [0.0] * (n + 1)
    for i in range(n):
        pre[i + 1] = pre[i] + r[i]

    s_sc = [None] * n
    for i in range(w + 1, n):
        s0 = i - w + 1                       # first return index in the window
        mu = (pre[i + 1] - pre[s0]) / float(w)

        x = [0.0] * (w + 1)
        acc = 0.0
        for k in range(w):
            acc += r[s0 + k] - mu
            x[k + 1] = acc

        m = w - 1                            # AR(1) pairs X_k -> X_{k+1}
        sx = sy = sxx = sxy = 0.0
        for k in range(1, w):
            p = x[k]
            q = x[k + 1]
            sx += p
            sy += q
            sxx += p * p
            sxy += p * q
        den = m * sxx - sx * sx
        if den <= 0.0:
            continue
        b = (m * sxy - sx * sy) / den
        a = (sy - b * sx) / m
        if b <= 0.0 or b >= 1.0:             # not an OU process at all
            continue
        tau = -1.0 / math.log(b)             # mean-reversion time, in bars
        if tau > tau_max:                    # kappa floor: reversion too slow
            continue
        ss = 0.0
        for k in range(1, w):
            z = x[k + 1] - (a + b * x[k])
            ss += z * z
        dof = m - 2
        if dof <= 0:
            continue
        vz = ss / float(dof)
        if vz <= 0.0:
            continue
        seq2 = vz / (1.0 - b * b)
        if seq2 <= 0.0:
            continue
        # X(win) is 0 by construction once beta is dropped, so this is
        # (X(win) - m_ou) / sigma_eq with X(win) = 0.
        s_sc[i] = (x[w] - a / (1.0 - b)) / math.sqrt(seq2)

    ctx.s = ctx.series(s_sc, "s_score")
    ctx._sbo = float(ctx.p.sbo)
    ctx._sso = float(ctx.p.sso)
    ctx._sbc = float(ctx.p.sbc)
    ctx._ssc = float(ctx.p.ssc)


def signal(ctx, i):
    s = ctx.s[i]
    if s is None:                            # kappa filter says stand aside
        return 0
    if s < -ctx._sbo:
        return 1
    if s > ctx._sso:
        return -1
    return 0


def exit_signal(ctx, i):
    """The paper's asymmetric closes - a short is covered further from zero
    than a long is sold - plus its stop: if the re-estimate no longer passes
    the kappa filter the residual has stopped mean-reverting and the reason
    for the position is gone."""
    if not ctx.positions:
        return False
    s = ctx.s[i]
    if s is None:
        return True
    if ctx.positions[0]["side"] == "long":
        return s > -ctx._sbc
    return s < ctx._ssc
